notes: PCT front page p001: INID fields (51), (11), (43), (21), (22), (30), (71), (72), (81), publication note, and both title renderings. The IMAGE_EXTRACT at line 32 is the front-page drawing of general formula (I); it is empty of molecules and is kept with the surrounding bibliographic block rather than opening the abstract, per the image rule.

The front page prints the abstract twice, once in English and once in German. Both renderings are inside this section; the German is the verbatim source of record, the English is the publication's own translation, not a machine one.

Page p002, the standard PCT two-letter country-code legend. The closed list has no fit: it is not bibliographic data about this application, it is boilerplate printed on every WO publication. Typed other deliberately rather than stretching bibliographic.

heading_text_zh: Beschreibung / Benzoylcyclohexandione, Verfahren zu ihrer Herstellung und ihre Verwendung als Herbizide und Pflanzenwachstumsregulatoren
heading_text_en: Description / Benzoylcyclohexanediones, processes for their preparation, and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators
notes: The description opens on p003. The Beschreibung heading and the invention title are folded into this section rather than given a stub section of their own; the field sentence proper is lines 54-55.
Prior art: JP-A 08 020554, JP-A 02 00222, WO 99/10327, WO 99/07688, WO 99/03845, then the stated disadvantages. Named publications only, no reagents and no procedure, so nothing here for A2.

The object (Aufgabe, lines 60-61), the solution statement, the drawing of general formula (I) at line 67, its (I) label, and the lead-in to the substituent definitions. Boundary against the next section is the line where the R1 definition starts.

R1, R2-R5, R6, R7 including both two-radical cases, R12, L, Y, Z, v, w, closed by the proviso on -L-R1. The IMAGE_EXTRACT at line 105 (p006) reports ten empty reactions; it sits mid-run and is kept with this section, never opening one.

Tautomeric forms when R6 is hydroxy, and the statement that base salts are likewise a subject of the invention. Typed summary_of_invention because it extends the claimed scope; it is not a substituent definition, so it is held out of the formula_definitions run on either side of it.

The glossary the Markush run depends on: Kohlenwasserstoff-Rest, chain radicals, cycloalkyl, halogen and haloalkyl, heterocyclyl, aryl, heteroaryl, the partially-or-fully-halogenated convention, the polysubstitution caveat, stereoisomers, the rule that Y and Z are not both heteroatomic, and the default that an unqualified 'optionally substituted' means substituted by R2.

heading_text_zh: Von naeherem Interesse sind Verbindungen der allgemeinen Formel (I), worin
heading_text_en: Of closer interest are compounds of the general formula (I), in which
notes: The five nested preference tiers, each opened by its own lead-in: von naeherem Interesse (162), bevorzugt (225), ebenfalls bevorzugt (246), besonders bevorzugt (278), ebenfalls besonders bevorzugt (287), ganz besonders bevorzugt (315). Kept as ONE section: they are successive narrowings of the same Markush definition, not different subject matter, and splitting them would give six sections that no later pass can join on. This is the longest single run in the document and the source of the very long substituent lines.

The general synthetic routes: Scheme 1 (II)+(III) to (I); Scheme 2 (IV) to (III) by two named routes, 2.1 base-catalysed with R1-H and 2.2 with R1-Li; Scheme 3 (V)+R1-Z2 to (III); Scheme 4 (Ia) to (Ib) by halogenation, (Ib) to (Ic) with nucleophiles, then oxidation of (Ic) to the sulfinyl/sulfonyl compounds. Counted 1+2+1+3 = 7 generic transformations. The closed list has NO type for a general-process/reaction-scheme block. Typed summary_of_invention because these schemes are the 'Verfahren zu ihrer Herstellung' half of the claimed contribution; they are emphatically not experimental_example, since no quantity, temperature or yield appears anywhere in them. contains_procedure is true because A2 should still read reactions out of them, but every one is generic (R-group placeholders, no amounts).

Excellent activity against a broad spectrum, the named monocot and dicot genera, the rice weeds, pre- and post-emergence behaviour, and the claim that economically important crops are damaged little or not at all. Typed beneficial_effects as the closest fit: it is prose asserting an advantage, with no numbers and no test protocol, so it is not assay_data. The measured percentages appear only in section C much later.

section_label: Use in Transgenic Crops and as Growth Regulator
notes: Transgenic crop prose: resistance traits, cited EP/WO/US patents for starch, glufosinate, glyphosate, sulfonylurea and Bt traits, molecular-biology technique references, antisense/cosuppression/ribozyme, compartment targeting, regeneration, then the closing statement that use in transgenic crops is also a subject of the invention, plus the growth-regulator paragraph at 465-466. The closed list has no fit for a use/utility block of this kind; typed other rather than stretching summary_of_invention over fifty lines of plant biotechnology.

Formulation types (WP, SP, EC, EW, SC, CS, DP, GR, WG, SG, ULV, microcapsules, waxes), how each is made, the auxiliary and literature references, and the active-ingredient content ranges. pharmaceutical_compositions is the only formulation type in the closed list; this is an agrochemical formulation, so the label is wrong but the meaning ('formulation content') is exactly right. contains_procedure is false: the manufacturing operations here are milling and mixing, not reactions.

The long alphabetical list of known herbicides that can be tank-mixed or co-formulated, acetochlor through the end of the alphabet, three of the longest lines in the document. Held out of the Formulations section because it is an enumeration of third-party actives, not a description of this invention's formulations; typed the same because it is still mixture-formulation content.

Dilution for use and the application rate, 0.001 to 10.0 kg/ha, preferably 0.005 to 5 kg/ha. Numbers without a procedure, but they are formulation-use parameters rather than activity measurements, so pharmaceutical_compositions is a better fit than assay_data.

ONE section spanning all nine numbered Schritt sub-steps, per the rule that an Example is one section however many sub-steps it prints; A2 decomposes it. Steps: 1 thiomethylation of 2,6-dichlorotoluene; 2 Friedel-Crafts acetylation; 3 tungstate/H2O2 oxidation to the sulfone; 4 hypochlorite haloform to the benzoic acid; 5 Fischer esterification; 6 NBS benzylic bromination; 7 cyclohexanolate displacement then ester hydrolysis; 8 acid chloride then O-acylation of cyclohexane-1,3-dione; 9 acetone-cyanohydrin-catalysed Fries-type rearrangement to the target. The 'Die nachstehenden Beispiele erlaeutern die Erfindung' lead-in and the 'A. Chemische Beispiele' part heading are folded in here rather than given a four-line stub section of their own.

ONE section spanning its three Schritt sub-steps: 1 phenoxide displacement on methyl 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-benzoate followed by ester hydrolysis; 2 acid chloride then O-acylation of cyclohexane-1,3-dione; 3 acetone-cyanohydrin rearrangement to the target. It branches off Example 1 step 6, which supplies the bromide.

Two things that govern every one of the seven tables that follow, not just Tabelle 1: the statement that the tabulated compounds were prepared, or are obtainable, analogously to Examples 1 and 2, and the abbreviation key (Ac, Bu, Bz, Et, Me, Pr, c, d, m, s, t, i, Fp., dd). Kept as its own section rather than folded into Tabelle 1 precisely because it applies to all of them; folding it in would have hidden the 'prepared analogously' statement from every later table.

10 parts by weight of a compound of formula (I) with 90 parts talc, ground in a hammer mill. The five Formulierungsbeispiele are given five sections, one each, on the same reasoning that gives Beispiel 1 and Beispiel 2 a section each: they are five separate examples, not sub-steps of one. contains_procedure is FALSE although a quantitative preparative procedure is present, because the field asks whether there is a REACTION procedure for A2 to read and there is none here; milling and mixing are not reactions. The 'B. Formulierungsbeispiele' part heading is folded in here.
25 parts active, 64 parts kaolin-containing quartz, 10 parts lignosulfonate and 1 part oleoylmethyltaurate, ground in a pin mill. Mixing only, no reaction, so nothing for A2.
20 parts active with Triton X 207 and further auxiliaries, wet ground. Mixing only, no reaction, so nothing for A2.
15 parts active, 75 parts cyclohexanone as solvent, 10 parts oxyethylated nonylphenol as emulsifier. Dissolution only, no reaction, so nothing for A2.

Two alternative recipes under one number: the 75-part fluidised-bed granulation, which runs across the p078 page break, and the 25-part colloid-mill/bead-mill/spray-tower route at line 871. Both are kept in this one section because the document numbers them as a single example 5. Granulation only, no reaction.

notes: Greenhouse protocol at 600-800 l/ha water volume and 1 kg a.i./ha, scored against untreated controls, with named compound numbers and percentage efficacies. Typed assay_data: compound identities paired with numeric activity and no reaction chemistry. contains_procedure is FALSE because the protocol here is a biological test, not a reaction A2 should read. Same greenhouse design applied at the three-leaf stage, with compound numbers and percentage efficacies. Biological protocol only, no reaction chemistry.

notes: Paddy-rice conditions with 2-3 cm standing water. The page break is not a section boundary and this section deliberately spans it. Biological protocol only, no reaction chemistry.
Selectivity trial reusing the protocols of biological examples 1 and 2 on a wider set of crops and weeds. Biological protocol only, no reaction chemistry.

Claims 1 to 13, opening on p081 (printed 79) and closing with claim 13 on p102 (printed 100). ONE section, not thirteen. THE CHECKED BOUNDARY: PDF pages p089 and p090 (printed 87 and 88, lines 978 to 987) carry doc_part='description' in their page comments, but they belong to the claims and are inside this section. Three pieces of whole-document evidence settle it, none of which a per-page reader could see. First, position: they sit between p088 and p091, both of which are claims pages, and the claim numbering is continuous across them, claim 2 opening at line 946 on p083 and claim 3 not opening until line 1009 on p092. Second, the enriched text's own continuation labels: line 980 is tagged 'Substituentenliste (Fortsetzung)' and line 990 on p091 is tagged 'continues from p90', so the substituent run is one unbroken list straddling all four pages. Third, the substituent sequence itself matches: p088 ends mid-list at Alkylsulfonyl, p089 resumes at Arylsulfonylamino and p090 at Heteroarylcarbonyloxy, the same order the description's own R2a list runs in at lines 191 to 201. The page-level classifier was misled because claim 2 reproduces the description's Markush list nearly word for word - lines 953-976 in the claims mirror lines 169-201 in the description - so on those two pages alone the claims and the description are textually indistinguishable. Concluded: claims, and the claims are one contiguous range 900-1141 with no description material inside them.

PCT/ISA/210 in English, pages p103 to p107: classification, fields searched, the X and A citations (US 4 954 165, WO 99 10327, JP 08 020554, US 4 957 538, JP 07 206808, DE 42 41 999), Box I and Box II observations, the ADDITIONAL MATTER sheet objecting that claims 1-12 cover a disproportionately large number of compounds, and the patent-family annex. Searcher Rufet, J, EPO, completed 2 November 1999.

Pages p108 to p112: the same search report reissued in German, same citations, same dates, same officer, same family annex. Held as a separate section from the English one rather than merged, because they are separate printed sheets in the publication and merging them would hide the duplication from any later pass that counts citations. A pass that treats the two as independent evidence would double-count every reference.
